html:
SMTO-POL-0026 — This approval request is out of date

GUID: 8e975b89-a06a-54e9-81e5-6490d48511bc
Slug: authority-checkpoint-conflict
Domain: POL · Subsystem: authority

What happened

  • The approval or question you answered isn't the one the Task is waiting on now. It was already answered, stopped or replaced, so SMTO didn't use your answer.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and open the conversation again. Your screen was showing an older approval than the one the Task is waiting on.
  2. Check the Task's activity to see whether the action already ran or was stopped, for example because it was answered in another window. Someone may already have approved or denied it, so you may not need to answer again.
  3. If an Approval needed card is showing, read what it asks, then select Approve once or Deny / stop task. SMTO only accepts a decision for the exact request that is waiting now.

What success looks like

  • The Task carries on after your decision, or no approval is waiting.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to answer the old approval again or delete the Task's history.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An authority decision (permission, capability, unsafe action, Activity approval or Agent Check override) did not match the current pending checkpoint: it was stopped, paused, already being handled, superseded, its request identity or digest changed, or another checkpoint is already pending.

What this means

  • Authority correlation found a stopped, handled, superseded or changed checkpoint, or a decision that no longer matches its pending request identity and digest. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Authority correlation found a stopped, handled, superseded or changed checkpoint, or a decision that no longer matches its pending request identity and digest.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh the retained task and compare authority request ID, activity, operation digest and current pause/stop state.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the run and read its current authority_requests and approval_pending state; submit a decision only with the current authority_request_id for the unchanged checkpoint. If the checkpoint was superseded, review the new pending request before deciding.
  • Refresh the task and review its current pending request before choosing an authority decision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate decision is accepted only for the unchanged current authority checkpoint.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
